tidbits.text: Locke published the year after England replaced King James II with William and Mary. His argument helped justify it.
tidbits.source_pointer: Casefile A, Day 2 (the names are outside the casefile)

tidbits.text: About 86 years later, Thomas Jefferson used the same logic in the Declaration of Independence: when a government destroys people's rights, the people may change it or get rid of it.
Document 2 says what people may do when power is abused. Document 4, Montesquieu, says how to build a government that can't abuse it. Used together, they make a bigger argument.
A 5 quotes only the few words that do the work, like "resume their original liberty," and explains the rest in its own words.

exemplars.text: In Document 2, Locke says a legislature that takes absolute power loses it, and the power goes back to the people, which shows people can take back a bad government.

In Document 2, Locke argues that a legislature grabbing "absolute power" forfeits its authority, which passes back to people with a right to "resume their original liberty." Paired with Montesquieu's warning in Document 4 that united powers destroy liberty, it shows the Enlightenment offered two answers to tyranny: take the power back, or build a government that can't seize it.
exemplars.what_changed: The 4 uses one document well. The 5 quotes only the words that matter and pairs a second document, so the evidence builds a bigger claim.

techniques.name: Short quote, your words
techniques.explanation: Quote three to six words that carry the idea, then explain them yourself. Long quotes hide your thinking.

techniques.name: Pair the documents
techniques.explanation: Put two documents side by side and say what they show together that neither shows alone.
